content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Sev 1 — GPU pool us-west-1.gpu-pool-3 reported 100% allocation and sustained queue growth, autoscale not triggering. Paging oncall for GPU-oncall rotation.
jamie_sre: on it. saw alerts for HPA target <custom/gpu_queue_length> not updating.
alice: confirm prometheus-adapter error spikes around 2024-11-05T13:02Z, adapter logs show 429s and 504s to prometheus.
jamie_sre: can someone check metrics-server and kube-apiserver for throttling? run quick checks please.
tyler_ml: looking at model-serving queue: backlog up from 200 -> 3.2k in 10m, tail latency > 8s, a bunch of low-priority batch jobs enqueued.
linda_support: we have customer 54B reporting timeouts for inference; CS alerted. I posted a triage note to the incident page.
jamie_sre: running commands now —
jamie_sre: ```
kubectl get hpa -n inference
kubectl get --raw /apis/custom.metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1 | jq .
kubectl logs -n monitoring prometheus-adapter-0 | tail -n 50
```
jamie_sre: HPA shows desired=0 current=0 for staged autoscalers because custom metric returns 0 or is missing. adapter logs: "error: upstream read timeout" and "rate limited by prometheus".
maria_infra: prometheus is showing a scrape backlog, our prometheus remote_write is also spiking. disk IO on prometheus-0 high, GC in flux.
alice: I see adapter returning 500s when hit with query range for series gpu_queue_length{pool="us-west-1.gpu-pool-3"}. stack traces point to scrape overlap and slow queries.
jamie_sre: immediate mitigation options: 1) manually scale the GPU node group (add N), 2) evict/scale down low-priority batch jobs, 3) point HPA to metrics-server fallback (not ideal), 4) route new requests to fallback hosted model for critical customers.
tyler_ml: we should enable fallback routing for high-SLA customers only. I can flip routing rule for customer 54B and a couple more.
maria_infra: manual node scale-up in progress, requesting +4 p3 nodes in us-west-1; will take ~7-9m to join. initiating autoscaling group increase now.
deploy-bot: manual-scaling: requested scaling group "gpu-us-west-1" to +4 instances. progress tracked in cloud console.
jamie_sre: evicting low-prio batch pods (namespace ml-batch) — will cordon one node and drain cheaper pods.
jamie_sre: ```
kubectl cordon node/gpu-node-22
kubectl drain node/gpu-node-22 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```
linda_support: sending hold message to affected customers: "We're investigating elevated latency on GPU-backed inference in us-west-1. We've activated mitigations and expect partial recovery in ~15-30 minutes. We'll update in 10 minutes or when we have a verified fix."
alice: prometheus adapter errors dropping after we limited heavy queries, but adapter still shows occasional 429. We need to clear query backlog and schedule long queries off peak.
tyler_ml: routing change completed for customer 54B and 22C to hosted-fallback-model. Verified reduced requests to the pool from those customers.
jamie_sre: node addition: 2/4 joined, kubelet registered, pods scheduling. queue growth slowed but still high (peak 1.4k).
maria_infra: continuing to investigate prometheus disk IO spike — possible compaction job. Throttling improved after prioritizing IO to head blocks; compaction paused for now.
jamie_sre: HPA now reads metric again but values delayed by ~30s. Desired replicas increased from 0 -> 8 but cluster autoscaler hasn't provisioned GPUs fast enough.
jamie_sre: short-term live mitigation: increase HPA maxReplicas to 12, enable burst capacity, and drain a couple more nodes to consolidate. Executing HPA patch.
jamie_sre: ```
kubectl patch hpa gpu-worker-hpa -n inference -p '{"spec":{"maxReplicas":12}}'
```
jamie_sre: patch applied. HPA desired scaling to 12 observed. cluster autoscaler queued new node requests.
onexistent-bot: (system) note: metrics latency means autoscale decisions delayed up to 90s.
alice: prom-adapter errors have reduced after we lowered QPS by delaying user analytics queries. But we should still treat adapter as a single point of failure for custom metrics.
tyler_ml: monitoring: rolling 1-min P95 latency dropped from 8s -> 3.1s after routers and node join.
linda_support: updating the incident page with timeline, customer impact, and mitigation steps. Notifying legal for any SLA hits from enterprise customers.
jamie_sre: prepare oncall handoff in 30m. summary for the next oncall: cause = delayed/lossy custom metrics pipeline (prometheus scrape/backlog + adapter rate limits) prevented HPA from seeing queue length => autoscaler didn't create GPUs in time => pool exhaustion and queuing. Mitigations applied: manual node scale-up (+4), HPA max increased to 12, evicted batch jobs, routing fallback for high-SLA customers, paused compaction on prometheus, limited heavy queries.
oncall-next: I'll take the handoff. next steps: monitor metric freshness, validate HPA stability, coordinate a proper postmortem with root cause and follow-up: - increase adapter resilience (caching/fallback), - add queue length fallback metric path, - autoscaler headroom for sudden spikes, - limit heavy analytics during high-load windows.
jamie_sre: thanks. I'll leave runbook notes and the commands we ran in the incident doc. tagging infra/maria, ml/tyler, support/linda for follow-ups.
linda_support: customer comms templated and sent to impacted accounts; CS will follow up if any SLA credits needed.
jamie_sre: marking incident as mitigated for active customer impact. keeping channel open for cleanup and postmortem. :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: canary update: fallback-route toggled for customers [54B,22C] -> success.
jamie_sre: last check: queue down to ~220, GPU utilization ~78%, HPA stable at 9 replicas, node pool at +4. leaving handoff to oncall-next.
oncall-next: acknowledged, will monitor for 2 hours and start postmortem draft.
incident-bot: incident update logged: severity lowered to S2. please file postmortem within 48h and tag "hpa-prom-adapter" and "gpu-autoscale".
